description: The plot illustrates how the “Harmful with Refusal Ratio” changes with sample size for two vision-language models evaluated on two benchmarks. The x-axis is labeled with sample sizes and uses a linear scale with four discrete tick values at 128, 256, 512, and 1024. The y-axis is labeled “Harmful with Refusal Ratio,” uses a linear scale, and spans from 0.0 up to about 0.55 with regularly spaced tick marks at 0.1 intervals. Four lines are shown: a blue solid line with circle markers (LlaVA-1.5-7B on FigStep) rising from about 0.20 at 128 to ~0.25 at 256, ~0.35 at 512, and ~0.36 at 1024; an orange solid line with square markers (Qwen2-VL-7B on FigStep) increasing from ~0.15 at 128 to ~0.23 at 256, then to ~0.42 at 512 and remaining at ~0.42 at 1024; a green solid line with triangle markers (LlaVA-1.5-7B on MMSafetyBench) increasing from ~0.06 at 128 to ~0.21 at 256, ~0.37 at 512, and ~0.38 at 1024; and a red solid line with diamond markers (Qwen2-VL-7B on MMSafetyBench) increasing from ~0.24 at 128 to ~0.26 at 256, ~0.43 at 512, and ~0.52 at 1024.
caption_used: The plot depicts the proportion of harmful responses accompanied by refusal tendencies across varying sample sizes for two vision-language models (VLMs) evaluated on two distinct benchmarks. The x-axis represents sample sizes (128, 256, 512, and 1024), while the y-axis quantifies the 'Harmful with Refusal Ratio,' ranging from 0.0 to 0.5. The blue line, corresponding to LlaVA-1.5-7B on FigStep, initiates at approximately 0.20 at a sample size of 128, steadily climbing to 0.34 by 512 before stabilizing. The orange line, representing Qwen2-VL-7B on FigStep, begins at roughly 0.15, escalates sharply to 0.42 at 512, and then plateaus. The green line, denoting LlaVA-1.5-7B on MMSafetyBench, starts at 0.08 and ascends gradually to 0.37 by 512, after which it remains constant. Notably, the red line, illustrating Qwen2-VL-7B on MMSafetyBench, commences at 0.25, surges to 0.45 at 512, and subsequently collapses to 0.48 by 1024, indicating a marked decline in refusal consistency. The legend clarifies the mapping of line styles to their respective model-benchmark combinations. Overall, Qwen2-VL-7B consistently outperforms LlaVA-1.5-7B in refusal ratios on both benchmarks, with the most pronounced divergence observed at larger sample sizes.
